prompt:
A clean, straight-on photo of a printed exhibition caption plate showing a transcribed expedition diary, headed 'FIELD DIARY - WINTER STATION' with the small line 'Fourteen entries, fourteen different closing letters'. Print EXACTLY 14 numbered lines (1. to 14.), each at least SIX words long, recording a day at a polar station.

CRITICAL WRITING LAW: the FINAL LETTER of each line's last word must be different from the final letter of every other line. Fourteen lines, fourteen distinct closing letters -- no letter may be used twice. Pick the last word of each entry deliberately.

Black text on a pale grey plate, nothing else.
easy_question: This image was supposed to show a printed page or log with numbered lines of text. Ignoring artistic quality and ignoring whether the wording is correct, does the image DEPICT that -- a printed page or board carrying a numbered list of text lines? A photo, a scan or a clean page all count as yes. Answer NO only if it is blank, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_read: This image is a page carrying 14 numbered lines of text. Transcribe the 14 numbered lines EXACTLY as written, in order. Copy every word, keep the original spelling, and keep the spaces between words. If a numbered line wraps onto a second printed row, keep it as ONE line. Separate one numbered line from the next with a single pipe character | and nothing else. Do NOT transcribe the title, any heading or any word bank. Do not add commentary, line numbers or quotation marks. Output only the transcribed lines separated by |.

Copy every word letter for letter, and keep each word's capital letters and small letters exactly as they are printed. Do not fix spelling, do not change the order of the words, do not add a word and do not leave one out. Leave out the title, any sub-heading, and any text that carries no number. Write out the list and nothing else.
